history.report:
Strategy code is back to the exact parent (verified 0.0624, per-seed identical). Summary:

**Change made and measured, then reverted.** I found a real self-contradiction in the bot: `draw_monster_priority_negative` paints a **-10 flee ring** around monsters the character is too hurt to duel, but `melee_monster_priority` returns **+1**, so the attack outranked the escape every turn — the retreat code is unreachable. The death traces confirm the consequence (seed 0: **36→0 of 46 HP over 20+ consecutive turns** against a goblin). I made the attack yield to the flee ring under a *relative* hurt test.

**Result: 0.0624 → 0.0671, but 3 seeds up / 2 down / 10 flat** — fails the "most seeds improve" bar, so I reverted it.

**The negative result is the valuable part:** retreating is structurally capped on this identity. The flee ring is radius 1, and 9 of 13 killers have `mmove 12` (max speed) — they close the one-square gap every turn, so distance never opens.

**Two findings that redirect the whole problem:**

1. **The score is the XP ladder, not depth.** `nethackers/arena/progress.py` scores `max(Dlvl:N, Xp:N, …)`, and on all 15 published seeds the winning term is `Xp:N` — never `Dlvl:N`. Seed 4 hit dlvl 7 (worth 0.0485) and scored 0.1791 = `Xp:10`. The depth ladder in GAME_RULES.md is the wrong target.
2. **XP is 73–97% from "normal" monsters** (goblins, jackals, gnomes) — only 1–8% from the `WEAK_MONSTERS` the bot currently coddles. So "never fight" would delete the XP economy.

I left `devtools/eval_harness.py`, which reproduces the published 15-seed table **bit for bit** (mean 0.0624; seed 3 matches 3052 turns/grid bug/0.0208) in ~90s, plus `experience.md` with four ranked leads — chiefly that the bot is gated behind `experience_level >= 8`, requiring ~400 dlvl-1 kills before it will touch a staircase.
